All 7 mixed headers are the bare noun the catalogue already uses for suggestions (Sugerencias / Suggestions / सुझाव / Подсказки / تجاویز / Gợi ý / 建议), so no new term is introduced. All 7 blocked sentences are impersonal statements of the rule, none an alarm or an imperative; all say 'open', never 'enter', so none contradicts the DuckDuckGo search row. Register matches each catalogue (es tú, fr vous, hi आप, ru вы, ur آپ, vi bạn, zh 你); the blocked sentence is subject-less like the other status lines. The label/empty/no-match strings still claim only local history — no string in this scope claims a session or a tab that the copy cannot support.

findings.observation: The 'state — title' separator is a spaced single em dash (U+2014 with U+0020 on both sides). All six other em-dash strings in this catalogue use the Chinese double em dash '——' with no spaces, including the same row pattern in browser_tab_strip.all_tabs_unshown and browser_url_bar.home_destination. A spaced Latin-width dash reads as a gap in Chinese typography on a row that renders on every keystroke.
findings.evidence: dash inventory of src/i18n/catalogues/zh-CN/ui.browser.json: 6 strings contain '——' (12 U+2014, all unspaced: download_refused, all_tabs_unshown, home_destination, latest_download, newest_download, site_unverified_certificate); this key contributes the only spaced pair. Prior audit 837ea3f0157c raised the same convention as M3 on the superseded value '已打开的标签页 — {title}': the value changed, the separator did not.
findings.disposition: fix with the suggested bytes; no meaning change

findings.observation: '网页地址' is understandable but '网址' is the standard Simplified-Chinese term for a web address, and it is shorter in a status line. The sentence is truthful either way; this is idiom only, not a mistranslation.
findings.evidence: counts over src/i18n/catalogues/zh-CN/ui.browser.json: 网址 = 0 keys, 网页地址 = 1 key (this one), 地址 = 10 keys. The catalogue uses bare 地址 for the address/URL concept (address bar, '此地址无法解析'), so 网页地址 is the only compound of its kind.
findings.disposition: optional; accept as-is if the author prefers the fuller compound

findings.observation: The context note enumerates the trigger as 'a blocked scheme (javascript:, data:, about:, an unknown scheme) or a file: URL', which reads as exhaustive, but the same notice is also shown for host-shaped input the classifier refuses as malformed (an out-of-range port or a rejected authority). A translator reading only the note would not know the sentence must also read as a general rule about what this field can open.
findings.evidence: browser-url-bar.tsx:436-442 sets refusedInput from suggestions.intent === 'blocked' || FILE_SCHEME.test(raw.trim()); address-autocomplete.ts:278-285 returns 'blocked' for 'an invalid port or a rejected authority'; the note under audit is ui.browser.context.json:1137-1141. The behaviour is correct — only the note's enumeration is narrower than the trigger set.
findings.suggested: Extend the note to name the malformed-address case (or prefix the list with 'for example'), e.g. '… a blocked scheme (javascript:, data:, about:, an unknown scheme), a file: URL, or a malformed address the browser cannot parse.' No translation changes needed: all 7 targets already state the general rule.
findings.disposition: optional wording fix; no re-translation required
